title: Embedding Fidelity Lighthouse: continuous golden-set evaluation & drift guard for rerank/embedding endpoints
creator: Aisha Mendoza
description: Build a reproducible evaluation harness (Embedding Fidelity Lighthouse) that runs nightly and on-demand to measure embedding accuracy and reranking quality across model variants. The harness must: 1) manage curated golden sets (global and customer-specific), 2) compute offline ranking/embedding metrics (MRR, NDCG@k, MAP@k, recall@k, average cosine similarity distributions), 3) detect drift using distributional tests and embedding-space distance shifts, 4) produce an observability dashboard and alerts with automated severity rules, and 5) scale to the hosted fleet and Dedicated customer buckets without impacting production inference latency.
acceptance_criteria: Nightly job runs for all active embedding models and stores results in metrics namespace:embeddings.fidelity.v1
Golden-set runner computes MRR@10, NDCG@10, MAP@5, recall@1/5 and mean cosine delta vs baseline for each model variant
Drift detector emits alerts when p-value < 0.01 for KS test on token-normalized-similarity distribution or when mean cosine delta > 0.05 from baseline
Dashboard shows model, dataset (global/customer/goldset id), run timestamp, key metrics and historical sparkline with regression highlighting
End-to-end harness imposes <5% additional cost on hourly inference bill for nightly checks (configurable sample size) and no runtime impact on live requests
Playbook outlines rollback criteria and automated canary gating if new model fails golden-set regression
tasks: Design golden-set schema and storage layout (global vs tenant-local, TTL, versioning)
Implement runner: vectorize queries, compute ranking metrics, store artifacts (golden predictions, embeddings snapshots)
Integrate drift tests: KS, Wasserstein, energy distance on embedding similarity distributions and a lightweight classifier-based drift score
Build ETL to sample representative query logs from production for nightly synthetic augmentations
Create Grafana dashboard and annotations; wire alerting to Slack and PagerDuty with escalation rules
Add RBAC and access control for customer-local golden sets in Private/Dedicated deployments
Benchmark harness resource usage and add autoscaling hints for Dedicated pools
notes: Trade-offs discussed in design review: full-run vs sampled-run. Decided on hybrid approach: full-goldens on release + nightly sampled checks for all models to limit cost.
We will normalize embeddings before distribution tests to avoid model size/quantization skew; keep both cosine and dot-product baselines for older models.
Considerations for multi-tenant: keep per-tenant baseline only for customers that opt-in due to storage and compliance.
Initial golden sets: 3 public corpora (Q&A pairs, semantic search queries, paraphrase ranking) + 12 customer-provided golds for early beta

implementation_plan: Phase 1 (2 weeks): golden-set schema, baseline runner, offline metric library, small pilot on 3 models
Phase 2 (2 weeks): drift detectors, production job orchestration, sampling ETL, automated report generation
Phase 3 (2 weeks): dashboards, alerts, RBAC, Dedicated autoscale guidance, beta with 5 customers
Phase 4 (ongoing): widen model coverage, per-tenant baselines, integrate into release gating and runtime-1.20 rollout
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Nightly runs could consume significant GPU capacity and raise costs. Mitigation: run embedding inference on burst/spot capacity, use cached KV prefixes and quantized model variants for checks.
Risk: False positives from noisy customer traffic. Mitigation: require sustained drift over 3 runs or classifier score before paging; surface confidence intervals in alerts.
Risk: Golden-set staleness. Mitigation: schedule review cadence and add synthetic perturbations to detect fragility across paraphrase variants.
Risk: Data privacy for customer goldens. Mitigation: store tenant-local golds encrypted, provide opt-in workflow, and purge TTL for temporary sets.
Risk: Metric mismatch across similarity metrics (cosine vs dot). Mitigation: compute both and surface delta; use cosine as canonical metric for normalized models.
